# Citation-Context Search — data pipeline (Member 1)

This folder holds the code that produces the data, splits and labels every
other member uses. The package is `citeds/`.

* **Shared data format:** [`SCHEMA.md`](SCHEMA.md). Read this first.
* **Data card, licenses, ethics:** [`DATA_CARD.md`](DATA_CARD.md)
* **Dataset statistics:** `docs/dataset_stats.md` (generated by the build)
* **Citation-function results:** `docs/citation_function_results.md` (generated by training)

## Setup

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q          # 23 tests, ~5 s, no data needed
```

## 1. Get the data (unarXive 2022)

Download unarXive 2022 JSONL shards from the links on
https://github.com/IllDepence/unarXive into `data/raw/`. Any folder layout
works: files are found recursively, and `.jsonl`, `.jsonl.gz`, `.jsonl.bz2`
and `.jsonl.xz` are all read.

**Start small.** Download a few monthly shards (for example 2020–2022),
build with `--max-papers 5000`, and share that with the team so they can
start. Then download everything and rebuild. Shards from other fields are
skipped automatically.

No data? Generate a synthetic file to check that everything runs. Its numbers
are meaningless.

```bash
python scripts/make_sample.py --out data/raw/sample --papers 400
```

## 2. Build tables, splits and leakage-controlled index contexts

```bash
python -m citeds.build --raw data/raw --field cs.CL --max-papers 5000
```

Writes to `data/processed/`:

| File | For whom |
|---|---|
| `papers.parquet` | everyone: the documents |
| `index_contexts.parquet` | Members 2 and 3: expansion text, leakage-controlled |
| `contexts.parquet` | stats and classifier only. **Never index this file** (it contains the queries) |
| `edges.parquet` | Member 4: PageRank, co-citation |
| `queries.parquet`, `qrels/qrels.{train,val,test}.txt`, `topics/topics.{train,val,test}.tsv` | everyone: evaluation |
| `build_info.json` | parameters and counts of the run |

The build ends with a leakage assertion and fails loudly if any query text is
still in the index. Settings (field, cap, seed, thresholds) are in
`citeds/config.py`.

## 3. Citation-function classifier (Naive Bayes)

Download SciCite (https://github.com/allenai/scicite) and put `train.jsonl`,
`dev.jsonl` and `test.jsonl` in `data/external/scicite/`. ACL-ARC jsonl files
work the same way; their 6 intents are mapped to 3 classes.

```bash
python -m citeds.citation_function train --data data/external/scicite
python -m citeds.citation_function predict            # -> data/processed/context_functions.parquet
```

Training picks the Naive Bayes alpha (Multinomial and Complement NB) and the
logistic-regression C on dev by macro-F1. It reports test accuracy, macro-F1,
per-class F1 and confusion matrices, along with a majority-class baseline,
in `docs/citation_function_results.md`.

## 4. Optional: fresh-paper crawler (OpenAlex)

> ⚠️ **CONTACT EMAIL PLACEHOLDER.** `citeds/config.py` ships with
> `CONTACT_EMAIL = "YOUR_EMAIL@example.com"`. The crawler **refuses to run**
> until you set a real address. Prefer an environment variable, which keeps
> it out of Git:
>
> ```bash
> export CITEDS_CONTACT_EMAIL=you@university.edu
> ```

```bash
python -m citeds.crawler --since 2024-01-01 --max 500
```

The crawler respects robots.txt, sends at most 5 requests per second, backs
off on 429 errors, and caches every response in `data/external/crawl_cache/`
so nothing is re-fetched. It skips papers already in `papers.parquet` and
writes `data/processed/fresh_papers.parquet`.
*It was not run against the live API during development, so try a small
`--max` first. If the OpenAlex filter in `citeds/crawler.py` returns nothing,
the concept or source IDs may have changed.*

## Using the data (Members 2–4)

```python
from citeds import io
papers  = io.load_papers()                 # paper_id, title, abstract, year, citation_count, ...
ctx     = io.load_index_contexts()         # leakage-controlled citation contexts
docs    = io.expanded_documents()          # paper_id, title, abstract, contexts, text (= expanded doc)
val_q   = io.load_queries("val")           # query_id, text, cited_paper_id, cited_citation_count, ...
edges   = io.load_edges()                  # citing_paper_id -> cited_paper_id
labels  = io.load_context_functions()      # context_id, function, confidence
io.qrels_path("test")                      # Path to TREC qrels
```

For Member 4: `citeds.leakage.assert_no_leakage(index_contexts, queries)` is
the check to run before reporting results.

## Layout

```
citeds/
  config.py             paths, seed, thresholds, crawler email (placeholder)
  schema.py             table schemas = team contract
  unarxive.py           streaming unarXive JSONL reader
  clean.py              marker/LaTeX removal, sentence splitting, ID normalisation
  tables.py             papers / contexts / edges + cleaning log
  splits.py             query sampling, train/val/test, TREC qrels/topics
  leakage.py            leakage control + assertion
  stats.py              dataset statistics report
  build.py              end-to-end CLI
  io.py                 loaders for teammates
  citation_function.py  Naive Bayes vs logistic regression classifier
  crawler.py            optional OpenAlex crawler
scripts/make_sample.py  synthetic unarXive-format sample (testing only)
tests/                  pytest suite
docs/                   schema, data card, generated reports
```

`data/` and `models/` are git-ignored, both for size and for licensing
(copyrighted full text is not republished). Share processed files through
the team drive.
